gems.name: UPI Reserve Pay (NPCI Single-Block-Multi-Debit), via Razorpay / Cashfree / PayU / Pine Labs
gems.what_it_is: A UPI rail. The buyer enters the UPI PIN once and blocks up to Rs 10,000 in their own bank account for up to 90 days. The merchant then debits exact amounts one or more times against that block, and anything unused is released. NPCI OC-228/2025-26 (8 Oct 2025) renamed SBMD to Reserve Pay. It also widened funding sources to SA/CA/OD/RuPay credit card/credit line and added user controls to view, update and revoke blocks.
gems.why_gem: It is the closest thing India has to a card authorisation hold, and it is legal. The money stays in the buyer's own account, not in POOL's or the PA's escrow, until the pool closes. Prior research put it in 'later', but three things have changed. It is now live on four PAs (Razorpay changelog 2025-10; Cashfree, PayU and Pine Labs docs). The NPCI circular says it is 'initially enabled for verified online merchants with low-ticket, high-frequency transactions', which is exactly what mutton/meat pools are. And UPI Collect was deprecated on 28 Feb 2026 (Razorpay changelog), so Intent/QR-based block-then-debit is the modern UPI pattern.
gems.use_in_pool: Mutton/meat and other pools under Rs 10k: 'Join pool' creates a Reserve Pay block for the buyer's maximum price. At pool close, POOL debits the winning bid price (Cashfree 'Raise Charge' / Razorpay debit), so there is no refund and no Wave Drop clawback, because the buyer only ever pays the final lower price. If the buyer walks away or the pool fails, POOL cancels the mandate and the block releases. The flow for appliances over Rs 10k is unchanged.
gems.replaces_or_adds: For small-ticket pools this replaces 'charge in full up front, then Wave Drop partial refund'. It adds a hold primitive that Razorpay Route does not have on the buyer side.
gems.license_or_pricing: Proprietary PA feature; activation through PA support; pricing not published.
gems.activity_evidence: Razorpay changelog entry 2025-10. NPCI OC-228 dated 2025-10-08. Cashfree docs list the flow Create Subscription -> Raise Authorisation -> Raise Charge -> Refund -> Manage Mandate. Pine Labs docs list Create Presentation API.
gems.maturity_risk: The Razorpay list of supported UPI apps is BHIM, INDmoney, Navi and Paytm. PhonePe and Google Pay are NOT listed, which cuts reach. Pine Labs says many banks allow only one active SBMD per customer. No PA documents sandbox/test-mode support. Nothing says whether it works with Route split transfers.

gems.name: Stripe extended authorization (card holds up to 30 days)
gems.what_it_is: A PaymentIntent with capture_method=manual and payment_method_options.card.request_extended_authorization=if_available. It keeps a card authorisation valid for up to 30 days instead of the usual 7. The capture_before field on the charge reports the real window.
gems.why_gem: Prior research limited US card holds to pools that close within about 5-7 days. Stripe's docs give a 30-day window on Mastercard for all merchant categories, and on Visa for all categories: Visa's effective window is 29 days 18 hours, with a 0.08% fee outside lodging and rental. The docs note that networks allow extended windows mainly when the final amount is unknown at authorisation, which is exactly POOL's case, since the price is set by sealed bids. Test cards 4242/5555/3782/6011 exercise it in test mode.
gems.use_in_pool: US pools with a buyer-chosen closing time of up to about 4 weeks. Joining places a real hold. At close, capture only the winning price with amount_to_capture; the remainder releases automatically, so there is no refund and no Wave Drop clawback on cards. Read capture_before to cap the closing-time picker for each buyer.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Extends the existing manual-capture plan. It removes the need to charge and then refund for pools longer than 7 days.
gems.license_or_pricing: Proprietary Stripe feature. Stripe says it is offered on IC+ pricing; blended-pricing accounts must contact support. There is an extra 0.08% per transaction in non-lodging categories.
gems.activity_evidence: Current Stripe docs page, fetched 2026-09-30, with the network table and test-card section.
gems.maturity_risk: Needs IC+ pricing or a support request on a live account. Amex and Discover extended windows are limited to travel/lodging categories. It is not available when Link is the payment method type. Longer holds can raise disputes, so a clear statement descriptor is needed.

gems.name: WhatsApp Business Platform Payments API (India) - Payment Gateway deep integration
gems.what_it_is: POOL sends a WhatsApp order_details (invoice) message. The buyer pays inside the chat with any installed UPI app, cards, netbanking or wallets. Payment status comes back through webhooks. There are two modes: UPI Intent (any PG, no refunds or status) and PG Deep Integration (Razorpay, PayU, Billdesk and Zaakpay only; refunds supported).
gems.why_gem: POOL is WhatsApp-first, and most teams assume WhatsApp can only send a payment link. Deep integration keeps the whole join-and-pay step in the chat on low-end Android, carries Razorpay notes/receipt fields back in payment signals, and supports refunds from the WhatsApp APIs.
gems.use_in_pool: 'Pool closed, your price is Rs X. Pay now' goes out as an order_details message inside the existing WhatsApp thread. The Razorpay payment_id links back to the pool order, and the Wave Drop refund is sent through the same integration.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds an in-chat checkout surface. It replaces sending a web payment link and bouncing the buyer to a browser.
gems.license_or_pricing: Proprietary (Meta plus the PG's fees). WhatsApp conversation pricing applies. PG MDR is unchanged.
gems.activity_evidence: Meta docs live on developers.facebook.com. The Razorpay blog has a '2026 merchant playbook' on WhatsApp payments, and 360dialog has partner docs.
gems.maturity_risk: Needs a verified WhatsApp Business account, with the PG account owner linking the PG in Meta Business Suite. The docs say nothing about sandboxes or limits. Compatibility with Razorpay Route transfers (dealer split with on_hold) is not documented, so check that the Order API can carry transfers[].

gems.name: pgledger
gems.what_it_is: A double-entry ledger implemented entirely as PostgreSQL tables, functions and views. There is no service to run. It provides accounts with currency and allow_negative/allow_positive balance flags, transfers, per-account versioned entries with previous and current balances, metadata, and reconciliation and multi-currency examples.
gems.why_gem: Created March 2025. It is the lightest-weight real ledger available. Prior research said to 'start with a Postgres double-entry schema' but offered no ready-made one. pgledger is that schema: ledger writes commit atomically with POOL's own order and pool rows in the same Postgres transaction, which Blnk, Formance and TigerBeetle cannot do because they are separate services. The author's HN-discussed post argues that double-entry ledgers are the missing primitive.
gems.use_in_pool: One account per buyer_hold:pool, dealer_payable, pool_rebate_reserve, pool_commission, psp_clearing (INR and USD separately). Every Razorpay or Stripe webhook becomes a pgledger transfer in the same database transaction as the state change. Setting allow_negative_balance=false on hold accounts blocks over-releasing dealer money. The reconciliation example guides the daily match against Razorpay and Stripe settlements.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces a hand-rolled ledger schema. It defers any need for TigerBeetle, Formance or Blnk.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free.
gems.maturity_risk: Pre-1.0 and maintained by one person. It has no built-in pending/two-phase transfers, so model holds as separate accounts. Vendor the SQL file into migrations and pin it.

gems.name: DBOS Transact (TypeScript)
gems.what_it_is: A library (npm @dbos-inc/dbos-sdk) that makes TypeScript functions durable by checkpointing each step in Postgres. It provides durable workflows, queues, scheduling, notifications and durable sleep. There is no separate orchestrator server.
gems.why_gem: Money flows need exactly-once behaviour across crashes, for example 'pool closes -> capture winner -> transfer to dealer -> partial refunds'. The obvious choices, Temporal and Inngest, add a server or a SaaS. DBOS runs in-process on the same Postgres as pgledger, so it is easy on five Windows laptops. It is very active: v5.0 on 2026-09-16, v5.2 on 2026-09-29, npm 5.2.11. It was featured on Show HN (DBOS Java, Nov 2025).
gems.use_in_pool: A workflow per pool: durable sleep until the buyer-chosen closing time, then close, pick the bid, capture or debit, run Route transfers on hold, and fan out Wave Drop refunds. Each step is checkpointed, so a crash never double-refunds. A delivery-code workflow waits on a notification and then releases the transfer hold.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces cron plus a BullMQ/Redis queue or a Temporal cluster for pool timers and payout sagas.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT; optional paid DBOS Cloud / Conductor.
gems.activity_evidence: 1,380 stars. Pushed 2026-09-29. Release v5.2 on 2026-09-29.
gems.maturity_risk: A smaller community than Temporal. The v5 major release is recent, so pin the version. Workflow code must be deterministic between steps.

gems.name: Dinero.js v2 (stable)
gems.what_it_is: An immutable, typed money library. Currencies are typed objects with a code, base and exponent (all 166 ISO 4217 currencies). It has a bigint entry point and an allocate() function that splits an amount by ratios without losing a paisa or cent.
gems.why_gem: v2 was stuck in alpha for years, so many developers assume it is unusable. v2.0.0 went stable on 2026-03-02 (npm latest 2.0.2). The release fixed allocate remainder distribution and added compile-time currency-mismatch errors, which stop INR and USD being added together by accident.
gems.use_in_pool: Wave Drop: allocate the rebate pool across buyers pro rata, with exact paise and cents so the sum always equals the refund total. Commission and dealer split per order. Showing prices in en-IN, hi-IN, te-IN and en-US formats.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces ad-hoc integer maths or big.js in the pricing and rebate code.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free.
gems.maturity_risk: The v1 to v2 API is a full rewrite (functional style), so older tutorials are wrong. Requires Node 20+.

gems.name: Hookdeck CLI
gems.what_it_is: A CLI that gives every developer free, permanent public webhook URLs and forwards events to localhost. Event history persists, and events can be inspected and replayed by teammates. It installs on Windows via scoop or npm.
gems.why_gem: The Stripe CLI covers Stripe, but Razorpay, Cashfree, WhatsApp Cloud API and PayU all need a public HTTPS URL to reach a dev laptop. Hookdeck's permanent URLs mean each of the five developers sets the Razorpay test-mode webhook once. Being able to replay a 'payment.captured' or 'transfer.processed' event is very useful when debugging hold and release logic.
gems.use_in_pool: One Hookdeck source per PSP per developer, routed to localhost:PORT/webhooks/razorpay and so on. Replay real test-mode events to reproduce Wave Drop and refund edge cases.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces ngrok or other tunnels with URLs that change on every restart.
gems.license_or_pricing: CLI Apache-2.0. Hookdeck says development use is completely free; production gateway is paid.
gems.activity_evidence: 363 stars. Pushed 2026-09-28. Release v3.0.3 on 2026-09-27. Show HN for Hookdeck Outpost (May 2025).
gems.maturity_risk: Low. Events pass through Hookdeck's cloud, so use only test-mode data.

gems.name: Marble (checkmarble)
gems.what_it_is: A self-hostable real-time decision engine for fraud and AML. It covers rule scenarios on your own data model, sanctions/PEP screening with continuous monitoring, a case manager, AI-assisted rule building and immutable audit trails. It runs with Docker Compose on 4 GB of RAM.
gems.why_gem: Most startups either buy Sift or Sardine (sales-led and expensive) or hard-code if-statements. Marble gives POOL a proper rules and case-management layer for its own mechanism risks, with a UI that non-engineers can tune, at zero licence cost for self-hosting.
gems.use_in_pool: Rules such as: many new buyers from the same device or IP joining one pool just before close (Wave Drop inflation); one dealer repeatedly winning with prices far below its own cost history (bait bidding); buyer accounts that always walk away after acceptance. Screen US and Indian dealers and beneficial owners against sanctions lists before payouts, and route hits to the case manager.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds a fraud and risk layer that the current stack does not have.
gems.license_or_pricing: Elastic License 2.0 (source-available; GitHub reports it as NOASSERTION). Free to self-host for internal use; paid enterprise features and SaaS.
gems.activity_evidence: 609 stars. Pushed 2026-09-21. v1.10.0 on 2026-09-21, v1.9.0 on 2026-09-07. SOC 2 Type II claimed in the README.
gems.maturity_risk: ELv2 forbids offering it as a hosted service to third parties, which is fine for POOL. A small community. It is overkill before real traffic, so add it once pools have real users.

gems.name: Didit (YC W26) identity verification
gems.what_it_is: A hosted KYC/KYB API. It covers ID document verification, passive or active liveness, face match, AML screening, proof of address, and phone/email checks, with SDKs for Web, iOS, Android, React Native and Flutter. It covers 220+ countries, including Indian documents (Aadhaar, PAN, Voter ID, passport) and US IDs.
gems.why_gem: It offers 500 full KYC checks per month free, with no card and no expiry, and publishes its per-check prices ($0.33 full KYC, $0.20 AML, from $2 KYB). Most competitors are sales-led and have minimums. One vendor covers both India and the US.
gems.use_in_pool: POOL's own 'Verified seller' badge: KYC of the dealer owner or representative plus AML screening before creating the Route linked account or Stripe connected account. Optional buyer re-verification for high-value appliance pools or flagged accounts.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds identity plus liveness, which Cashfree Secure ID's GSTIN/PAN/bank checks do not cover. For India it is a candidate replacement for HyperVerge or Signzy.
gems.license_or_pricing: Proprietary SaaS. 500 free checks per month, then published per-check prices; the UIDAI lookup is $0.25 per answered attempt.
gems.activity_evidence: Launch HN 'Didit (YC W26)' on 2026-03-10. Public pricing page verified 2026-09-30.
gems.maturity_risk: A young company ($2M seed per its own marketing). Aadhaar-based verification in India has UIDAI and legal constraints; prefer DigiLocker consent flows or PAN checks until counsel signs off. Data residency for Indian PII is unverified.

gems.name: Sandbox.co.in (by Quicko) tax and KYC API stack
gems.what_it_is: An Indian developer API platform. It offers GSTIN search and verify, 'Track GST Returns' (a GSTIN's filing history), GSTIN-by-PAN, PAN verify and PAN-Aadhaar link status, penny-drop and penny-less bank verification, MCA company and director master data, DigiLocker and EntityLocker consent sessions, GST e-invoice/IRN and e-way bill through the IRP, GSTR-2A/2B/9, and TDS calculation and filing. It has separate test and production environments, Postman collections and GitHub SDKs.
gems.why_gem: One Indian API covers both verifying the dealer and POOL's own tax paperwork. 'Track GST Returns' is a strong real-world seller-trust signal (a dealer that actually files GSTR-1/3B) that most seller-onboarding stacks miss. MCA director data checks that the person onboarding really runs the company.
gems.use_in_pool: Dealer onboarding: GSTIN verify + return-filing check + PAN + penny-less bank name match + MCA director match, then the 'Verified seller' badge. Later: e-invoice generation for POOL's commission invoices and reconciling the TCS/TDS credits POOL deducts as an e-commerce operator.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Can replace Cashfree Secure ID for dealer KYC, and partly replaces the ClearTax GSP plan with one vendor.
gems.license_or_pricing: Proprietary. Pricing is behind a cost calculator or sales; a third-party source mentions a 14-day free trial. Not independently confirmed.
gems.activity_evidence: Live docs with llms.txt index, changelog and status page. Operated by Quicko.
gems.maturity_risk: Prices are not public. GSTR-8 (e-commerce operator TCS return) and section 194-O were not found in the docs index, so POOL's own TCS filing may still need a CA or GSP. Test-environment data is simulated.

gems.name: Hyperswitch Prism (stateless payment connector library)
gems.what_it_is: A connector library extracted from Juspay Hyperswitch. One request schema is translated to many processors' APIs. It has no database, stores no PII and has no vault. The npm package is hyperswitch-prism; SDKs also exist for Python, Java and Rust.
gems.why_gem: Prior research marked its Razorpay coverage as unverified. The generated connector matrix in the repo now shows 'Razorpay V2' as supported for most flows, alongside Stripe, Adyen, Cashfree (partial), PhonePe and PayU. It is also shipping quickly: v0.2.0 in June 2026, v0.4.0 on 2026-09-04, v0.5.0 on 2026-09-25. So one TypeScript pay-in interface for India and the US is becoming realistic without running full Hyperswitch.
gems.use_in_pool: Only for the buyer pay-in, refund and status layer behind POOL's own PaymentProvider interface, so a second Indian PA can be added as a failover. Keep Route transfers, Stripe Connect transfers and Reserve Pay as direct SDK calls.
gems.replaces_or_adds: A possible later replacement for a hand-written adapter layer. It does not replace Route or Connect.
gems.license_or_pricing: Apache-2.0, free.
gems.activity_evidence: 1,400 stars. Pushed 2026-09-30. v0.5.0 on 2026-09-25 (npm modified the same day). The parent Hyperswitch repo shows 45,262 stars via the GitHub API.
gems.maturity_risk: Pre-1.0. It has no split, marketplace, hold/transfer or payout abstraction ('Beyond payments' is listed as an aspiration). Its connector table uses ⚠ and ? for many flows. Too early to depend on for the demo.

gems.name: ThumbmarkJS
gems.what_it_is: An MIT-licensed browser fingerprinting library that runs on the client with no backend. There is an optional hosted API with a free tier that adds TLS/HTTP server-side signals, bot, VPN, TOR and datacenter detection, and a threat score.
gems.why_gem: It is a free, lightweight device signal for POOL's biggest mechanism-abuse risk: fake or duplicate buyers inflating a pool to trigger a Wave Drop or a better tier. The fingerprint feeds straight into Marble rules. The big-name alternative (Fingerprint Pro) is paid at scale.
gems.use_in_pool: Store a device hash on join-pool, bid-view and payment events. Flag pools where several 'different' buyers share a device hash and phone-number pattern, and require OTP or KYC step-up for them.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds a device signal to the fraud rules.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT library; hosted API has a free tier, with paid plans above it.
gems.activity_evidence: 1,157 stars. Pushed 2026-09-25. v1.12.0 on 2026-09-25. The README claims 60,000+ sites use it.
gems.maturity_risk: The README itself says the client-only library reaches about 80% uniqueness. Identical low-end Android phones on the same carrier may collide, so use it only as one signal and never to block a buyer on its own.

gems.name: Kintsugi (US sales tax / global nexus monitoring)
gems.what_it_is: An AI-assisted sales tax platform. The free plan provides nexus monitoring for the US plus 100+ countries, AI product categorisation and a Stripe integration. Filings cost $75+ each with no transaction fees. The tax estimate API (POST /v1/tax/estimate, TypeScript SDK @kintsugi-tax/tax-platform-sdk) is on the Premium plan.
gems.why_gem: Stripe Tax charges per transaction. For a thin-margin US marketplace, a free tool that alerts on nexus and charges per filing rather than a transaction percentage can be much cheaper once real US volume exists.
gems.use_in_pool: After a US pilot: connect Stripe for free nexus monitoring across states, and use Kintsugi for registration and filing as a marketplace facilitator if it proves cheaper than Stripe Tax filing.
gems.replaces_or_adds: A possible later alternative to Stripe Tax's filing and registration features. Keep Stripe Tax for demo-time calculation.
gems.license_or_pricing: Free plan $0; Starter $75+ per filing or registration; API/SDK only on custom Premium.
gems.activity_evidence: Pricing and API pages live, fetched 2026-09-30.
gems.maturity_risk: The calculation API is paywalled, so it is not useful for the prototype. Support for marketplace-facilitator rules was not confirmed on the pages fetched.

gems.name: DBOS Transact (TypeScript) - @dbos-inc/dbos-sdk
gems.what_it_is: A durable-execution library that runs inside our own Node process and keeps all workflow state in our existing Postgres. It has checkpointed workflows and steps, durable sleep, and queues with worker and global concurrency, rate limits, priority, deduplication, partitions and timeouts. It also has cron schedules that run exactly once per interval (the idempotency key is schedule name + time), and send/recv, setEvent/getEvent and streams between workflows.
gems.why_gem: The current stack (06_prototype_stack.md) plans Temporal Cloud for money flows plus BullMQ + Valkey for jobs. That is three extra systems, and Temporal adds its own cloud region question. DBOS is only a library plus Postgres: no separate server and nothing extra to run on Windows. v5.2 shipped on 2026-09-29, the project is 3 years old, and it ships SDKs for TS, Python, Go, Java and Rust. Queue rate limits map directly onto WhatsApp and SMS send limits.
gems.use_in_pool: One engine for all of POOL's timed and money flows. (1) A pool-close workflow: DBOS.sleep until the closing time the buyer chose, then settle bids and run the Wave Drop partial refunds. (2) A payment-hold saga that waits for the payment-aggregator webhook (recv with a timeout), then waits for the delivery/pickup code, then releases the split settlement, with automatic compensation on timeout. (3) A rate-limited queue for WhatsApp notifications. (4) Cron jobs for dealer reminders and reconciliation. Workflow IDs are idempotency keys, so a replayed payment webhook cannot double-release money.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces Temporal Cloud, BullMQ and Valkey, cutting 3 moving parts. Postgres becomes the only stateful dependency.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT library, 'free forever' to self-host. The optional Conductor dashboard/recovery is DBOS Pro at $99/mo (1M checkpoints), Teams at $499/mo, Enterprise can self-host Conductor.
gems.activity_evidence: 1,380 GitHub stars; v5.2 released 2026-09-29; npm @dbos-inc/dbos-sdk 5.2.11 published 2026-09-29; repo pushed 2026-09-29.
gems.maturity_risk: Smaller community than Temporal. Workflow code must be deterministic, and side effects must go in steps. The data region of Conductor SaaS is not stated, so skip Conductor or self-host it to keep India data in India. Not tested on PGlite (see unverified).

gems.name: PGlite + pglite-socket (Postgres in WASM, no Docker)
gems.what_it_is: Real Postgres compiled to WebAssembly, running as an npm package in Node. pglite-socket (the `pglite-server` CLI) exposes it on a TCP port, so node-postgres, postgres.js and psql connect as if to a normal server. Extension packages include pgvector, pgmq, pg_textsearch, pg_uuidv7, pg_ivm, PostGIS and pgtap, plus 30+ contrib modules including pg_trgm, citext, pgcrypto and unaccent.
gems.why_gem: Most teams assume Windows developers need Docker Desktop for Postgres. PGlite gives each of the 5 Windows developers, and each Vitest worker, a throwaway real Postgres with the same extensions POOL uses in production (pgvector, pg_trgm), all from `npm install`. Its extension catalogue grew in 2025-2026 and now includes pgmq and pg_textsearch.
gems.use_in_pool: `pglite-server --db=./.pgdata --port=5432` in the dev script. Each test file gets a fresh in-memory database, with Drizzle migrations applied before the tests run. Also usable for seeded demo databases in investor-demo rehearsals.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces Docker Desktop and Testcontainers for local dev and CI unit/integration tests. Production stays on managed Postgres.
gems.license_or_pricing: Apache-2.0, free
gems.activity_evidence: 16,098 stars; @electric-sql/pglite 0.5.8 (2026-08-26); pglite-socket 0.2.11 (2026-08-26).
gems.maturity_risk: One underlying connection, multiplexed. The docs say 'not all cases might be covered', and SSL is not supported. Heavy concurrency, LISTEN/NOTIFY-dependent libraries and advisory-lock behaviour should be checked against a real Postgres in CI. Pre-1.0 version numbers.

gems.name: Node.js 24.12 LTS native TypeScript (type stripping, now stable)
gems.what_it_is: Node runs .ts files directly by stripping type annotations, with no tsx, ts-node or build step. This was marked stable in v24.12.0 and v25.2.0.
gems.why_gem: Many developers still set up tsx, nodemon or ts-node pipelines, which are often flaky on Windows because of path, ESM and watcher issues. Node 24.12 LTS removes that layer, and this development machine already runs Node v24.12.0.
gems.use_in_pool: Run API servers, DBOS workers, seed scripts and migration scripts with `node --watch src/server.ts`. Type checking stays in `tsc --noEmit` in CI and in the editor. Set `erasableSyntaxOnly` in tsconfig so nobody writes enums or namespaces, which stripping cannot handle.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces tsx, ts-node and nodemon for backend dev and scripts. Front-end bundling (Next.js/Turbopack) is unchanged.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free
gems.activity_evidence: Stable status in the v24.12.0 LTS and v25.2.0 release lines (Node docs and release notes). Verified locally: node v24.12.0 is installed.
gems.maturity_risk: Only erasable syntax is supported: no enums, namespaces or parameter properties. It does not type-check. Path aliases need Node subpath imports (`#imports`), not tsconfig paths.

gems.name: oRPC (with Hono as the HTTP host)
gems.what_it_is: A typed RPC framework. You define a procedure once with Zod, Valibot, ArkType or any Standard Schema, and get end-to-end TypeScript types to the client, generated OpenAPI plus REST routes, contract-first mode, typed errors, SSE streaming via async iterators, and TanStack Query integration. Adapters exist for Hono, Next.js, Node, Bun and fetch.
gems.why_gem: It combines tRPC's developer experience with real OpenAPI, which tRPC does not give. That matters because POOL needs both a typed web/mobile client and a documented public API for dealers, brand desks and the POOL MCP server. Hono, the host, had the top satisfaction scores in the State of JS 2025 backend section.
gems.use_in_pool: One contract package in the monorepo covering createPool, joinPool, placeSealedBid, acceptOffer and confirmDeliveryCode. The buyer web app and dealer console use the typed client. The same contract publishes OpenAPI for dealer integrations and is wrapped by the POOL MCP server. SSE streams drive live pool countdowns and join counts on low-end Android without WebSocket infrastructure.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces hand-written REST routes, separate OpenAPI docs and a separate tRPC layer. It adds a single source of truth for the API.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free (Hono is also MIT)
gems.activity_evidence: middleapi/orpc: 5,653 stars, pushed 2026-09-30; @orpc/server 1.15.4 stable (2026-09-23); v2.0.0-beta.40 in progress. Hono: 32,387 stars, 4.13.11 (2026-09-29).
gems.maturity_risk: v2 is in beta and the docs site shows @beta install commands. Pin 1.15.x for the prototype and plan the v2 migration. It has a smaller ecosystem than tRPC.

gems.name: pgledger (double-entry ledger in pure Postgres SQL)
gems.what_it_is: A double-entry bookkeeping ledger built only from Postgres tables, functions and views. You install SQL files (two vendored ULID helpers + pgledger.sql) and call functions for accounts and transfers. Each entry records the account's previous and current balance, supports balance history at any point in time, and handles multi-currency through liquidity accounts.
gems.why_gem: Marketplaces that hold money usually either build a fragile 'balance' column or adopt a separate ledger database (TigerBeetle, Formance). pgledger writes ledger entries in the same Postgres transaction as order state, so the order status and the money records cannot drift apart. It is a Postgres-centric gem most TS teams never find.
gems.use_in_pool: An internal mirror of money held by the licensed payment aggregator, per pool and currency (INR, USD). Accounts: buyer_booking_held, order_escrow, seller_payable, pool_fee_revenue, wave_drop_pot. A delivery-code confirmation moves order_escrow to seller_payable and pool_fee_revenue in the same transaction that marks the order delivered. Wave Drop refunds move wave_drop_pot to buyer_refund. The ledger gives investors provable, reconcilable numbers.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds a proper internal ledger. It replaces ad-hoc balance columns and avoids a separate ledger service. It does not replace the payment aggregator, which still holds the real money.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free
gems.activity_evidence: 494 stars; created 2025-03-12; release v0.7.0 on 2025-12-03; repo pushed 2026-09-30. Author's write-ups on pgrs.net (2025-03, 2025-06).
gems.maturity_risk: Small, single-maintainer project. No TS SDK: tests are in Go, so we call its SQL functions through Drizzle `sql`. The README does not document idempotency or negative-balance rules, so we add our own idempotency-key table. Pin the SQL version inside our migrations.

gems.name: pg_textsearch (true BM25 inside Postgres) - via Tiger Cloud Mumbai or PGlite
gems.what_it_is: A Postgres extension from Tiger Data (Timescale) for BM25-ranked full-text search. The index lives in normal Postgres pages (WAL, replication and pg_dump all work) and uses Block-Max WAND for fast top-k queries. Syntax: `ORDER BY content <@> 'query'`. Combined with pgvector it gives hybrid search in one database.
gems.why_gem: The stack currently lists Meilisearch as a separate search service. pg_textsearch went from a preview (Oct 2025) to 1.0 GA and now v1.4.0 (2026-08-18). Relevance-ranked search is now possible without a second system, and it pairs with pgvector plus Voyage embeddings for product matching.
gems.use_in_pool: Search for canonical products and open pools (for example 'LG 7kg front load', 'Sunday mutton Kukatpally'), fused with pgvector similarity for fuzzy product-link matching. It runs in PGlite for local dev.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces Meilisearch, removing one moving part and one sync pipeline.
gems.license_or_pricing: PostgreSQL licence, free. Managed: Tiger Cloud, which has regions in ap-south-1 Mumbai and us-east-1 and a free plan.
gems.activity_evidence: 4,007 stars; created 2025-07-06; v1.4.0 on 2026-08-18; pushed 2026-09-30; PG 17 and 18 supported, PG 19 beta best-effort.
gems.maturity_risk: The biggest catch is availability. It is not on Supabase (0 hits in the supabase/postgres repo) and not in PlanetScale's extension list, so it only works if POOL's database is on Tiger Cloud or self-hosted. It uses Postgres text-search configurations, which have no Telugu or Hindi stemmer; the 'simple' configuration must be used for those scripts and quality tested. Until then, pg_trgm + pgvector is the fallback that works on every host.

gems.name: PlanetScale Postgres (Mumbai + US, $5 single-node entry)
gems.what_it_is: PlanetScale's managed Postgres, launched in 2025 (the company was long known only for MySQL/Vitess). It offers Postgres 18.6 and 17.11 with pgvector 0.8.5, pgvectorscale 0.9.0, pg_cron 1.6.7, PostGIS 3.6.4, pg_partman, pg_trgm and hypopg. A PS-5 single node costs $5/month (announced 2025-10-30); 3-node HA starts at $30/month.
gems.why_gem: Most people still think of PlanetScale as MySQL-only. For POOL it means one vendor with both AWS ap-south-1 (Mumbai, slug 'ap-south') and us-east. That gives India data residency plus a US region at prototype prices, with pgvector and pg_cron built in. Alternatives checked: Neon has no Mumbai region (nearest is Singapore), and Fly.io has no Mumbai region.
gems.use_in_pool: Two separate databases: India (Mumbai) and USA (us-east-1). Each runs DBOS workflows, pgledger and pgvector product matching in its own region. $5 nodes for demos, upgraded to HA before real pilots.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces two self-managed AWS RDS instances for the prototype, simplifying the setup.
gems.license_or_pricing: Commercial SaaS. From $5/mo per single-node database; HA from $30/mo.
gems.activity_evidence: Extension docs list PG 18.6/17.11 (fetched 2026-09-30); $5 plan blog dated 2025-10-30; the regions page lists AWS ap-south-1 and us-east-1.
gems.maturity_risk: The regions page does not show which engine is available in each region, so confirm Postgres in ap-south in the dashboard before committing. No pgmq, pg_net or pg_textsearch. Logical replication (needed for Zero/Electric) is not verified. The single node has no failover.

gems.name: Absurd (durable workflows = one SQL file + thin SDK)
gems.what_it_is: A durable-execution system by Armin Ronacher (Earendil). The whole engine is one absurd.sql of stored procedures, and workers pull tasks from Postgres. It has step checkpoints, retries, sleep, and race-free waiting on events. SDKs: TypeScript (npm absurd-sdk), Python, and experimental Go. It also has the absurdctl CLI and the Habitat dashboard.
gems.why_gem: It is even smaller than DBOS: no extension and no service, so it works on any managed Postgres (RDS, PlanetScale, Supabase). Earendil has run it in production for five months (per the 2026-04-04 post). It is a credible fallback if DBOS's API feels heavy.
gems.use_in_pool: Backup choice for the same jobs as DBOS: pool-close timers, waiting for the delivery-code event, Wave Drop payout. Pick one engine; do not run both.
gems.replaces_or_adds: An alternative to DBOS; like DBOS, it would replace Temporal, BullMQ and Valkey.
gems.license_or_pricing: Apache-2.0, free
gems.activity_evidence: 2,449 stars; created 2025-10-20; release 0.5.0 on 2026-08-04; npm absurd-sdk 0.5.0.
gems.maturity_risk: Pre-1.0. No built-in cron or queue rate limits documented (DBOS has both). Smaller team.

gems.name: Zero by Rocicorp (sync engine over Postgres)
gems.what_it_is: A general-purpose sync engine. The zero-cache service keeps a SQLite replica fed by Postgres logical replication. Clients write ZQL queries that answer instantly from a local cache and then update live.
gems.why_gem: It reached 1.0 in June 2026 after two years of alpha, and 1.9.0 shipped today (2026-09-30), so it is no longer the 'experimental' tool many people assume. It gives instant, live UI without writing WebSocket or realtime code.
gems.use_in_pool: The dealer console: live list of open pools in the dealer's category and area, joins updating in real time, and the dealer's own bid status. The buyer's 'my pools' screen. Other dealers' sealed bids must never be in a synced query; they are enforced server-side, so restrict Zero to non-secret tables.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds realtime sync. It replaces hand-built WebSocket/SSE fan-out for dashboards.
gems.license_or_pricing: Apache-2.0; self-host zero-cache
gems.activity_evidence: rocicorp/mono 3,398 stars, pushed 2026-09-30; @rocicorp/zero 1.9.0 (2026-09-30); 1.0 covered by InfoQ June 2026.
gems.maturity_risk: Adds a stateful service (zero-cache) and needs wal_level=logical on PG 15+. Not verified on PlanetScale. Sealed-bid privacy makes permission mistakes costly. For the prototype, oRPC SSE may be enough.

gems.name: Electric (Postgres Sync) + TanStack DB
gems.what_it_is: Electric streams 'shapes' (filtered subsets of Postgres tables) over plain HTTP, which a CDN can cache. TanStack DB 0.6+ adds client-side persistence and live queries on top. Durable Streams/StreamDB extend this to event streams.
gems.why_gem: Because it is HTTP and CDN-friendly, it suits flaky mobile networks in India better than long-lived sockets. Electric Cloud pricing (April 2026) is $1 per million writes with free reads and fan-out, and pay-as-you-go bills under $5/month are waived.
gems.use_in_pool: Read-only live views: a public pool page showing member count and time left, shared over WhatsApp links and cached at the edge, and order-tracking proof timelines.
gems.replaces_or_adds: An alternative to Zero for realtime reads. Adds offline-tolerant live views.
gems.license_or_pricing: Apache-2.0 (Electric, @electric-sql/client); TanStack DB MIT; Electric Cloud pay-as-you-go from $0
gems.maturity_risk: TanStack DB is pre-1.0. Electric Cloud regions are not confirmed. Needs logical replication. Pick at most one of Zero or Electric.

gems.name: Workflow DevKit ('use workflow') with Postgres World
gems.what_it_is: Vercel's open-source durable-workflow SDK, written as plain async TypeScript functions marked with the 'use workflow' and 'use step' directives. Its Postgres World backend (built on pg-boss) runs self-hosted on any long-running Node server, with an observability UI.
gems.why_gem: It fits a Next.js 16 team naturally, and it is not locked to Vercel: Postgres World runs anywhere.
gems.use_in_pool: Alternative for pool-close and settlement workflows if the team wants workflows written inside the Next.js app.
gems.replaces_or_adds: An alternative to DBOS/Temporal.
gems.license_or_pricing: Apache-2.0, free self-hosted
gems.activity_evidence: 2,441 stars; created 2025-10-23; npm `workflow` 4.8.9 stable; v5.0.0-beta.58 on 2026-09-29; @workflow/world-postgres 4.3.7.
gems.maturity_risk: Relies on compiler transforms (harder to debug on Windows). A major v5 is in beta, which means churn. Newer than DBOS.

gems.name: PgQue (zero-bloat Postgres event queue, PgQ reborn)
gems.what_it_is: Skype's PgQ architecture rebuilt in pure SQL/PL-pgSQL for managed Postgres. It uses snapshot batching and TRUNCATE-based table rotation, so no dead tuples build up. Each consumer has its own cursor (Kafka-like fan-out). A pg_cron ticker drives it, and there is an npm `pgque` client.
gems.why_gem: SKIP LOCKED queues bloat under sustained load, and this avoids that. It works on RDS, Supabase and Neon without C extensions. Built by Nikolay Samokhvalov (Postgres.ai).
gems.use_in_pool: A transactional outbox and event bus: bid placed, pool closed, code verified. Each event fans out to independent consumers (WhatsApp notifier, analytics, search indexer) inside the same Postgres.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Would replace Kafka/Redis Streams for event fan-out. It does not replace DBOS for workflows.
gems.license_or_pricing: Apache-2.0 (includes ISC-licensed PgQ code), free
gems.maturity_risk: Early API (0.x). Delayed messages not shipped. Needs pg_cron. Probably overkill at prototype volume.

gems.name: Microsoft pg_durable (durable workflows inside Postgres, in SQL)
gems.what_it_is: A Postgres extension, open-sourced by Microsoft in 2026, that runs checkpointed durable workflows written in SQL inside the database, with retries, fan-out and recovery. It uses a background worker.
gems.why_gem: A strong signal that durable execution is moving into Postgres itself. Worth tracking for the settlement flows later.
gems.use_in_pool: Not for the prototype. It may later run database-side jobs such as settlement batching or Wave Drop calculation.
gems.replaces_or_adds: A future alternative to app-level workflow engines.
gems.license_or_pricing: PostgreSQL License, free; managed only on Azure HorizonDB
gems.maturity_risk: Labelled 'Preview'. PG 17/18 only. No Windows source install. No TypeScript client. Needs extension install and a background worker, so it does not work on most managed hosts (including PlanetScale and Supabase as checked).

gems.name: Claude API built-in tools, now GA: web_fetch_20260318 + citations + structured outputs / strict tool use + SDK toolRunner
gems.what_it_is: Server-side features of the Claude API, used from the official @anthropic-ai/sdk (v0.129.0, MIT, 28 Sep 2026). Web fetch reads a URL or PDF for Claude. The newest version (web_fetch_20260318) can filter the page with code before it reaches the context, and takes allowed_domains/blocked_domains, max_uses, max_content_tokens and citations. Structured outputs (output_config.format, GA since 29 Jan 2026) and strict tool use guarantee the output matches a schema. The SDK ships zodOutputFormat() and messages.parse(), plus a .toolRunner() agent loop with Zod tool helpers.
gems.why_gem: Most people still think of these as beta add-ons. The Feb to Aug 2026 changelog moved web fetch, web search, code execution, Files API and Agent Skills out of beta. Web fetch costs nothing beyond tokens, and code execution is free when used with web search or fetch. With citations switched on, every product fact Claude reports points to a passage on the source page. That is 'AI helps, never invents' built into the platform, with no agent framework on top and no second model provider.
gems.use_in_pool: 'Paste any link' pipeline. Call messages.parse() with a Zod ProductIdentity schema (brand, model, variant, GTIN if the page shows it, pack size, seller-page price), with web_fetch set to citations:on, max_uses:3 and an allowed_domains list during the demo. Each field keeps its citation, and a field without one is shown to the buyer as 'unconfirmed'. The same toolRunner loop handles the seller-side 'draft my bid' helper. Labels and invoices go straight to Claude vision (high-resolution image input arrived with Opus 4.7).
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces a separate agent framework and scraping-plus-LLM glue for the main product identification flow. Adds page-level citations as the anti-hallucination guarantee.
gems.license_or_pricing: SDK: MIT. Web fetch has no extra charge beyond tokens. Setting inference_geo to 'us' costs 1.1x. The only geos are 'us' and 'global' (no India region, verified on the data-residency docs today).
gems.activity_evidence: @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.129.0 published 2026-09-28. Release notes show web fetch without a beta header since 17 Feb 2026, structured outputs GA 29 Jan 2026, Files API and Skills GA 19 Aug 2026.
gems.maturity_risk: Web fetch does not run JavaScript (the docs say so). Many Amazon.in and Flipkart pages render with JS or block bots, so a fallback is needed (see Parallel Extract, or the GA browser use tool, which runs in our own browser). The tool caches pages unless use_cache:false.

gems.name: Parallel Web Systems: Extract API + Task API with 'Basis' (per-field citations + calibrated confidence)
gems.what_it_is: Web API built for AI agents. Extract turns any public URL (including JS-heavy pages and PDFs, per its docs) into markdown excerpts focused on an 'objective'. The Task API fills a JSON schema you define. Every field comes with a 'Basis': citations, reasoning, source excerpts and a calibrated confidence score. There is a TypeScript SDK (parallel-web on npm).
gems.why_gem: Less famous than Firecrawl or Tavily, and the only one we found that returns a confidence score and citations for each field of a structured record. That matches POOL's honest-options rule directly: a low-confidence field is shown as unconfirmed instead of guessed. The Basis framework now covers the cheapest processors too (Lite and Base).
gems.use_in_pool: Fallback when Claude web_fetch gets an empty or JS-only page. Step 1: Extract (about $0.001 per request) gets clean page text, which goes back to Claude for identification. Step 2, optional: the Task API Lite processor returns GTIN/model/variant with a confidence score. Any field below a threshold asks the buyer to confirm. Claude stays the only reasoning model; Parallel only fetches and grounds.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces building or maintaining our own headless-browser scraping farm or proxy setup for the prototype. Adds per-field confidence.
gems.license_or_pricing: SDK: MIT. Extract $0.001 per request. Task API $5 to $2,400 per 1,000 runs depending on processor. Free: up to 5,000 requests a month, plus signup credits (the page says up to $80) and $5 a month.
gems.activity_evidence: parallel-web npm 1.3.4 published 2026-09-29. SDK repo pushed 2026-09-30 (26 stars; the company is much bigger than its SDK star count).
gems.maturity_risk: Not verified whether Extract works reliably on Flipkart or Amazon.in product pages. We must test with 20 real links before relying on it. It is a third-party data processor for buyer-pasted URLs, which is low sensitivity.

gems.name: Voyage AI voyage-4 family + voyage-multimodal-3.5 (+ rerankers)
gems.what_it_is: Embedding and reranking models. Voyage-4 (blog dated 15 Jan 2026) has large, standard, lite and an open-weight nano model that share one embedding space, so vectors from different sizes can be compared. Voyage-multimodal-3.5 embeds mixed text and images, and video too. Official TS SDK: voyageai (MIT). Anthropic's own embeddings guide names Voyage because Anthropic has no embedding model.
gems.why_gem: Anthropic effectively recommends it, so it keeps POOL within the Claude-only rule. The multimodal model lets us match a product photo plus its title to the same canonical product, which text-only embeddings cannot do. Because of the shared space, cheap voyage-4-lite can index the catalogue while voyage-4-large handles queries. Each model's first 200M tokens are free.
gems.use_in_pool: Product entity resolution. Every identified product (title + main image) is embedded into pgvector. When a new link arrives we search nearest neighbours, rerank, and let Claude make the final same/different call with a strict-schema tool. That is how two buyers pasting a Flipkart link and an Amazon.in link for the same pressure cooker land in the same pool. It also powers 'similar pools near you'.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds a proper matching layer instead of fuzzy string matching on titles. Replaces any need for OpenAI or Cohere embeddings.
gems.license_or_pricing: voyage-4 $0.06/M tokens, lite $0.02/M, large $0.12/M, 200M free tokens each. Multimodal-3.5: $0.12/M text tokens, $0.60 per billion pixels, 150B pixels free. Reranker rerank-3-lite $0.02/M.
gems.activity_evidence: Pricing page updated 2026-09-29. voyageai npm 0.4.0 published 2026-06-15. Named in the Claude docs embeddings guide.
gems.maturity_risk: Low for the API. The TS SDK is small (46 stars) but thin; plain fetch also works. Embeddings are processed in the US.

gems.name: zxing-wasm (ZXing-C++ compiled to WebAssembly)
gems.what_it_is: Typed ES/CJS module that reads and writes 1D and 2D barcodes (EAN-13/UPC/GTIN, QR, DataMatrix) in the browser, Node or Bun, with no server round-trip.
gems.why_gem: The best 'AI never invents' step is often no AI: a GTIN read off the barcode is certain. Label identification needs no model call and works offline in a low-end Android browser, where the native BarcodeDetector API is patchy. A small, well-maintained project that people rarely think of in an AI stack.
gems.use_in_pool: (1) 'Scan the pack' as an alternative to pasting a link. The GTIN becomes the product key, and Claude only fills in descriptive fields. (2) Showing and scanning the delivery/pickup code as a QR at handover, which triggers release of the held payment. (3) The seller scans GTINs when listing bid inventory.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds deterministic product identity. Replaces relying on vision OCR of barcodes, or a paid barcode SDK.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free
gems.activity_evidence: 277 stars. npm 3.1.4 published 2026-09-10. Repo pushed 2026-09-29.
gems.maturity_risk: Single-maintainer wrapper around ZXing-C++, which is mature. The WASM file is about 1 MB, so lazy-load it only on the scan screen.

gems.name: Sarvam AI speech: Saaras v4 (STT) + Bulbul v3 (TTS) + Sarvam-Translate
gems.what_it_is: Bengaluru lab's Indic speech APIs. Saaras v4 does speech-to-text for 22 Indian languages plus English, with modes transcribe/translate/verbatim/translit/codemix, auto language detection, and keyterm prompting (up to 50 terms). It accepts OGG/Opus, the WhatsApp voice-note format. Bulbul v3 does TTS in 11 languages including te-IN and hi-IN, with 30+ voices. Sarvam-Translate covers all 23 languages. JS SDK on npm: sarvamai.
gems.why_gem: v4 is newer than most comparisons people cite (many still compare Saarika/v2). Codemix mode and keyterm prompting are exactly what Telugu-English grocery or meat-shop speech needs ('2 kg mutton curry cut, boneless'). It costs about ₹30 per audio hour, INR-billed and Indian-hosted. Claude remains the reasoning model; Sarvam only converts speech to and from text.
gems.use_in_pool: WhatsApp-first India flow. A buyer sends a Telugu voice note, Saaras v4 (codemix) produces text, and Claude maps it to the product and quantity or a pool action with a strict tool schema. Keyterms are the current pool's product names. Bulbul v3 reads the pool status and closing time back as a Telugu or Hindi voice reply for low-literacy users. Sarvam-Translate can cross-check Claude's Telugu UI strings and notifications.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces Google/Azure STT for Indic speech. Adds a voice input and output channel.
gems.license_or_pricing: Commercial API. STT ₹30 per hour, TTS ₹3 per 1,000 characters, translation ₹0.004 to 0.005 per character. Free signup credits that do not expire. The npm package has no licence field.
gems.activity_evidence: sarvamai npm 1.1.10 published 2026-09-09. Official plugin inside LiveKit agents-js (@livekit/agents-plugin-sarvam 1.9.1, 26 Sep 2026).
gems.maturity_risk: The REST STT limit is 30 seconds per request; longer voice notes need the batch or streaming API. The LiveKit plugin README still shows bulbul:v2 in examples. We should run our own Telugu word-error-rate test on 30 real voice notes before committing.

gems.name: Sarvam Vision 2.1 (Digitize + Extract APIs)
gems.what_it_is: 3B-parameter document vision-language model for OCR in 22 Indian languages plus English. Version 2.1 (released 24 Sep 2026) adds key-value and form extraction, complex multi-page tables and Indic handwriting recognition. It is served as a Digitize API (layout-faithful markdown/HTML) and an Extract API (key-value fields).
gems.why_gem: Released 6 days ago. On Sarvam's own new Indic OCR Bench it reports 87.39% across 22 languages, and it reports 87.3% on olmOCR-Bench. These are the vendor's figures and still need independent confirmation. The handwriting and key-value support fits the hard Indian cases: handwritten meat-shop bills, Telugu shop-establishment certificates, FSSAI and GST documents.
gems.use_in_pool: Verified-seller onboarding. The seller photographs their FSSAI licence, GST certificate or trade licence. The Sarvam Extract API pulls licence number, name, address and validity. Claude checks consistency against what the seller typed and flags mismatches for human review. It can also read handwritten delivery challans for proof-based order tracking.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces generic OCR (Google Vision, Textract) for Indic-script documents. It complements Claude vision, which handles English and typed documents well.
gems.license_or_pricing: Commercial API. Digitisation ₹0.50 per page, Extraction ₹1.00 per page.
gems.activity_evidence: Blog dated 2026-09-24. Listed on the models page of docs.sarvam.ai today.
gems.maturity_risk: Very new release, and the benchmarks are the vendor's own. Test on 50 real Hyderabad documents first. Seller documents are personal data, so we need a DPDP-compliant consent and retention policy.

gems.name: LiveKit Agents for Node (agents-js) + LiveKit Connectors (WhatsApp Business Calling)
gems.what_it_is: Apache-2.0 TypeScript framework for realtime voice agents, with official plugins for anthropic (built on the official @anthropic-ai/sdk) and sarvam, plus Deepgram, ElevenLabs, Silero VAD and others. Connectors (GA on LiveKit Cloud, 1 Sep 2026) bring WhatsApp Business Calling and Twilio calls straight into a LiveKit room with no SIP trunk. WhatsApp inbound works natively over WebRTC; outbound works where Meta allows it.
gems.why_gem: Most voice-agent advice points Indian teams to Python (Pipecat or Bolna). This is TypeScript-native for our 5 TS developers, already has Claude and Sarvam plugins, and since this month answers WhatsApp calls directly. WhatsApp is how Indian users actually call businesses. Meta's rate for business-initiated calls to India was reported at about $0.005 per minute (third-party report, not checked with Meta), and user-initiated calls are free to the business.
gems.use_in_pool: 'Call POOL on WhatsApp' demo. A Telugu-speaking buyer or meat-shop owner taps call on WhatsApp. Sarvam STT feeds a Claude agent with POOL tools (join pool, check pool status, confirm a bid), and Bulbul TTS replies. The same agent can make outbound 'your pool closes in 1 hour' calls in the US over Twilio.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds a voice channel. Replaces a Python voice stack or a closed no-code voice platform.
gems.license_or_pricing: agents-js: Apache-2.0. Connector minutes cost the same as SIP: $0.004/min on the Ship tier, $0.003/min on Scale. Concurrent connector-call limits: 5 on Build, 20 on Ship, 100 on Scale.
gems.activity_evidence: agents-js 938 stars, @livekit/agents 1.9.1 published 2026-09-26, repo pushed 2026-09-30. Connectors blog dated 2026-09-01.
gems.maturity_risk: Connectors only work on LiveKit Cloud, not self-hosted. WhatsApp calling needs a verified WhatsApp Business number with calling enabled, which the founder must set up. A community forum thread shows projects must request the connector be enabled. The anthropic plugin pins an older SDK range (^0.33.1); check it supports the Claude model we use.

gems.name: DBOS Transact (TypeScript)
gems.what_it_is: Library that makes TypeScript functions durable by checkpointing each step in Postgres. If the process crashes, workflows resume from the last completed step. It also provides durable queues with rate limits, concurrency and dedup, durable sleep and scheduling, and notifications. It needs only Postgres: no Temporal cluster, broker or separate server.
gems.why_gem: Durable execution is what makes agent runs and money flows safe, and most teams reach for Temporal (heavy on Windows) or a hosted service. DBOS runs inside our own Node process with only the Postgres we already have. Version 5.2 shipped yesterday. The README explicitly targets AI-agent workloads with non-deterministic APIs.
gems.use_in_pool: The pool lifecycle as one durable workflow: open, then a durable sleep until the buyer-chosen closing time, then collect sealed bids, run a Claude step to explain the options, notify buyers, wait for accept or walk-away, capture payment, release on the delivery code, and compute and issue Wave Drop partial refunds. Each Claude call and each Razorpay/Stripe test-mode call is a checkpointed step, so a crash never double-refunds or loses a pool close. A rate-limited queue keeps us within Anthropic and WhatsApp limits.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces cron jobs, BullMQ/Redis and home-made retry code. It is an alternative to Temporal or Inngest. A comparable newer option is Vercel's Workflow SDK (npm 'workflow' 4.8.9, Apache-2.0, 2.4k stars, created Oct 2025).
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free. The optional DBOS Conductor dashboard is commercial.
gems.activity_evidence: 1,380 stars. v5.2 released 2026-09-29. @dbos-inc/dbos-sdk 5.2.11 on npm.
gems.maturity_risk: Every workflow step must be deterministic or idempotent, which needs team discipline. Fewer stars than Temporal, but backed by a company and actively released.

gems.name: mcp-use (TypeScript MCP server + MCP Apps widgets + inspector)
gems.what_it_is: Full-stack MIT framework for building MCP servers and clients in TypeScript. It has typed tools, resources and prompts, React UI widgets that follow the MCP Apps / Apps SDK formats, a built-in /inspector, hot reload, built-in OAuth 2.0 working with any identity provider, and a create-mcp-use-app scaffold.
gems.why_gem: Far easier than the raw @modelcontextprotocol/sdk for shipping an MCP server that shows interactive UI inside Claude or ChatGPT. It grew to 10.7k stars in 18 months and publishes releases almost daily. Lighter alternatives with the same verification: xmcp (MIT, 1.3k stars) and FastMCP (MIT, 3.3k stars).
gems.use_in_pool: An investor 'wow' moment. A POOL MCP server with tools find_pool(product_url), join_pool(pool_id, qty), pool_status and my_orders, plus a widget card showing the live pool (price tiers, time left, joined count). A buyer then joins a pool from inside Claude or ChatGPT. Payment still happens on POOL's own payment-aggregator checkout page, never inside the chat. Later it can be listed in the official MCP Registry (registry.modelcontextprotocol.io, v1.8.1).
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds an agentic-commerce distribution channel. Replaces building a raw MCP server and OAuth by hand.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT. Optional hosted cloud (Manufact) is paid.
gems.activity_evidence: 10,699 stars. mcp-use npm 2.7.1 published 2026-09-28.
gems.maturity_risk: Moves fast and has had breaking changes between major versions. MCP Apps client support differs between Claude and ChatGPT. This is not needed for the core prototype; build it after the main flow works.

gems.name: Laminar (lmnr) — agent observability, evals, 'Signals'
gems.what_it_is: Open-source (Apache-2.0, Rust backend, YC S24) observability platform for AI agents. One-line OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation of the official Anthropic TS SDK (Laminar.initialize({instrumentModules:{anthropic:Anthropic}})). It shows traces with token usage, cost and tool calls, an evals SDK and CLI, SQL dashboards, and data labeling. 'Signals' let you describe a failure in plain English (for example 'agent guessed a GTIN without a citation') and get alerted when it happens.
gems.why_gem: Less famous than Langfuse, which ClickHouse acquired in Jan 2026 and which stays MIT and self-hostable. Laminar is agent-centric: session transcripts, trace search, and an MCP/CLI so Claude Code can debug from our traces. Signals turn our 'never invents' rule into a production alarm. The free tier (1 GB, 7-day retention) is enough for the prototype, and it self-hosts with docker compose.
gems.use_in_pool: Trace every product identification, bid explanation and voice turn. Signals: 'product field without a citation', 'agent quoted a price not in the seller bid', 'Telugu reply contained English fallback'. We can show investors a live trace of AI grounding.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds LLM tracing, cost tracking and evals. Alternative to Langfuse, LangSmith or Braintrust.
gems.license_or_pricing: Apache-2.0 self-host. Cloud: Free $0 (1 GB, 7-day retention, 1 seat), Starter $30/month, Pro $150/month.
gems.activity_evidence: 3,287 stars. Release v0.2.5 on 2026-09-13, repo pushed 2026-09-29. @lmnr-ai/lmnr 0.8.49 published 2026-09-23.
gems.maturity_risk: Smaller company than Langfuse. Keep the instrumentation OpenTelemetry-standard so we can switch to Langfuse (@langfuse/otel 5.11.1) if needed. Traces contain buyer messages, so mask phone numbers and addresses.

gems.name: vitest-evals (by Sentry)
gems.what_it_is: Vitest extension for LLM and agent evals. It provides a suite API, judges, tool-call replay, a JSON report with a local React report UI, and a GitHub Actions reporter that writes check-run annotations.
gems.why_gem: The obvious choices changed in 2026. OpenAI announced it would acquire Promptfoo on 9 Mar 2026; it says it will stay open source but it now sits inside a competitor of our model provider. Evalite's stable release has not moved since Nov 2025 (0.19.0; 1.0 is still in beta, last beta Feb 2026). vitest-evals is Apache-2.0, released this month, and runs inside the test runner our TS team already uses, so evals gate pull requests like unit tests.
gems.use_in_pool: A golden set of 100 real product links (Flipkart, Amazon.in, Amazon.com, D2C sites, meat-shop listings), each with the expected product identity. CI fails if identification accuracy drops or any field appears without a citation. Also: 30 Telugu/Hindi voice-note transcripts mapped to the expected pool action, and bid-explanation outputs checked by a Claude judge for 'mentions only prices present in the bids'.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds regression testing for the AI features. Replaces Promptfoo or Evalite as the default TS eval harness.
gems.license_or_pricing: Apache-2.0, free
gems.activity_evidence: 349 stars. npm 0.17.0 published 2026-09-10, repo pushed 2026-09-10. Maintained by Sentry.
gems.maturity_risk: There are ready-made harness adapters for ai-sdk, openai-agents and pi-ai, but none for the raw Anthropic SDK; we would write a thin custom harness (small job). Pre-1.0 API.

gems.name: Kapso (WhatsApp Cloud API developer platform + TS client + MCP)
gems.what_it_is: Official Meta Business Partner that wraps the WhatsApp Cloud API: messages, templates, interactive lists and buttons, WhatsApp Flows, webhooks and human handoff. It offers a free shared sandbox number, a CLI, an MCP server, agent skills, and an MIT TS client (@kapso/whatsapp-cloud-api). Voice calling routes to Pipecat agents.
gems.why_gem: Found through Show HN (Dec 2025). The free shared sandbox number lets all 5 developers build and test the WhatsApp agent flow before Meta business verification of POOL's own number is finished, which is a common multi-week blocker. The TS client is thin, typed and MIT-licensed.
gems.use_in_pool: Prototype the WhatsApp-first India flow: a buyer forwards a product link to the POOL number, the Claude pipeline identifies it, and the reply is an interactive list of matching pools plus a 'Start pool' button that opens a WhatsApp Flow to pick the closing time. Move to POOL's own verified number when it is ready.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Alternative to Twilio or Gupshup-style BSPs for the prototype. Adds sandbox testing and MCP tooling.
gems.license_or_pricing: Client: MIT. Platform: Free $0 (2,000 messages/month, 1 number, $2 credit), Pro $25/month (100k messages), Platform $299/month. Meta conversation fees are separate.
gems.activity_evidence: @kapso/whatsapp-cloud-api 0.3.0 published 2026-08-05 (217 stars). Show HN 2025-12-23. Backed by the Platanus accelerator.
gems.maturity_risk: Small startup focused on Latin America. India-specific pricing and support are not confirmed. Its native voice calling supports only Pipecat (Python); for TS voice use LiveKit Connectors. Keep a thin adapter so we can switch BSP.

gems.name: Flue (agent harness framework from the Astro team, now at Cloudflare)
gems.what_it_is: Apache-2.0 TypeScript 'agent harness' framework: like Claude Code, but headless and programmable. Agents are functions ('use agent') built from useModel, useTool, useSkill (Markdown SKILL.md) and useSandbox. It includes durable sessions, subagents, MCP client, OpenTelemetry, a Postgres adapter and channels. Deploys to Node, Cloudflare Workers, Render or CI. Claude is reached through pi-ai, which depends on the official @anthropic-ai/sdk.
gems.why_gem: Created Feb 2026 and already at 8.4k stars and v2.2.2 (released 28 Sep 2026). It is the newest serious TS option and fits Claude's skills-based way of working better than Mastra, which routes models through Vercel AI SDK providers rather than the official Anthropic SDK.
gems.use_in_pool: Only if POOL needs an autonomous back-office agent: for example a 'catalogue steward' that nightly re-checks pooled products and seller listings against their source pages, with skills written in Markdown that the founder can edit. It is not needed for the buyer-facing flow.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Alternative to Mastra, VoltAgent or LangGraph.js for long-running autonomous agents.
gems.license_or_pricing: Apache-2.0, free
gems.activity_evidence: 8,402 stars. Created 2026-02-07. @flue/cli 2.2.2 released 2026-09-28. Pushed 2026-09-28.
gems.maturity_risk: Very young and changes quickly (v1 beta to v2.2 in about 8 months). It calls Claude indirectly through pi-ai, so check that this meets our 'official Anthropic SDK only' rule. Do not put it on the investor-demo critical path.

gems.name: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) + official js-sdk
gems.what_it_is: Open standard (Apache-2.0) launched 11 Jan 2026 by Google and Shopify, with more than 70 supporters listed on ucp.dev (including Stripe, Visa, Mastercard, PayPal and Amazon). It lets AI agents discover products and complete checkout. It has an MCP binding and works with AP2 (Agent Payments Protocol) payment handlers. Spec release v2026-08-25; official JS SDK.
gems.why_gem: If buyer-side AI assistants start shopping for users, pooled demand is a natural product to expose to them. Being early helps with US investors. In India, Reuters reported (1 Sep 2026) that NPCI is preparing a UPI protocol for agent payments, not yet formally announced.
gems.use_in_pool: Watch for now. Later, expose POOL pools as UCP-discoverable offers ('join this pool at the per-buyer guaranteed price'), with checkout handed to Stripe Connect (US) or the Indian payment aggregator. It pairs with the mcp-use server.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds a future distribution channel. Nothing to replace now.
gems.license_or_pricing: Apache-2.0
gems.activity_evidence: ucp repo 3,405 stars, pushed 2026-09-29, release v2026-08-25. js-sdk 48 stars, pushed 2026-09-24.
gems.maturity_risk: The spec is still changing. There is no India or UPI mention on ucp.dev. Agent-initiated payments in India depend on an NPCI framework that is not final. Do not build on it for the pitch prototype.

gems.name: Infisical Agent Vault
gems.what_it_is: Self-hosted Go credential proxy for AI agents. The agent sends HTTP requests containing placeholder secrets (for example __anthropic_api_key__), and the proxy swaps in the real credential on the way out, so the agent never sees the key. It has a TS SDK for minting short-lived tokens, SQLite or Postgres storage, and a management UI.
gems.why_gem: Show HN, Apr 2026 (156 points). It solves a real risk for a 5-developer team using Claude Code and agents next to Razorpay and Stripe test keys: prompt injection from a scraped product page cannot exfiltrate a key the agent never had.
gems.use_in_pool: Development: developers' coding agents and any POOL agent that calls external APIs go through Agent Vault with test keys, so the keys never appear in prompts, logs or traces. Production rule: payment actions stay in deterministic code, not in agent tools.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds a secret-isolation guardrail. Complements the .env and secret-manager setup.
gems.license_or_pricing: Core MIT (enterprise directory under a commercial licence; GitHub shows NOASSERTION because of this mixed licence).
gems.maturity_risk: Its README says it is in active development and the API may change. It is a MITM proxy, so its TLS setup on Windows developer machines needs care.

unverified: Parallel Extract success rate on Flipkart / Amazon.in / Myntra product pages: not tested. Docs claim JS-heavy pages work, but anti-bot behaviour on Indian marketplaces is unknown.
Sarvam Vision 2.1 benchmark numbers (87.39% Indic OCR Bench, 87.3% olmOCR-Bench) are the vendor's own. Not independently reproduced.
WhatsApp Business Calling India rate ($0.005/min, business-initiated) comes from a third-party blog (campaignhq/respond.io), not Meta's pricing page.

Bolna (github.com/bolna-ai/bolna, MIT, 779 stars, YC F25, $6.3M seed Jan 2026): India-focused voice orchestration with Exotel/Plivo-style telephony. Not verified whether it supports Claude/Anthropic as the LLM, and it is Python, so we excluded it as a gem.

Indian no-code voice platforms found on Product Hunt 2026 (Bolcho AI, ThinnestAI at ₹1.5/min, Vomyra, TalkStack): claims not verified on their own sites. They are closed platforms and probably do not fit the Claude-via-official-SDK rule.
Bhashini (Govt of India) free ASR/TTS/translation APIs: current developer access terms, rate limits and Telugu quality not verified today.
GS1 India DataKart / Verified by GS1: public developer API access and pricing for GTIN-to-product lookup not confirmed. It seems to need a GS1 membership or partner agreement.

Claude Managed Agents (public beta since Apr 2026, with webhooks, session budgets and scheduled deployments per the release notes): not evaluated in depth. Beta status makes it unsuitable for the pitch critical path.
Official MCP Registry (registry.modelcontextprotocol.io, repo v1.8.1 Aug 2026): whether it is preview or GA could not be confirmed from the site.

Claude MCP connector (calling remote MCP servers from the Messages API) is still beta (header mcp-client-2025-11-20) and not eligible for zero data retention. Noted, not recommended for the prototype.

Headroom (headroomlabs-ai/headroom, Apache-2.0, 74k stars, TS compress() library): context compression could cut tokens on large product pages, but lossy compression conflicts with 'never invent'. Not tested on product pages, so left out.

gems.name: Uniwind (Tailwind v4 engine for React Native)
gems.what_it_is: A build-time Tailwind CSS v4 engine for React Native from CodeMask, the team behind Unistyles. It works with Expo, iOS, Android and Web. You write the same className strings as on the web.
gems.why_gem: It was created in July 2025 and most teams still default to NativeWind. It already has about 1.04M weekly npm downloads (week of 22-28 Sep 2026). HeroUI Native and React Native Reusables now both build on it. It parses Tailwind 4 and CSS at build time, so styles are not parsed on every render. The vendor's own benchmark claims about 2.4x faster than NativeWind (Android 94ms vs 227ms); treat that as a vendor claim, but it matters on low-end Android.
gems.use_in_pool: The one styling layer for the Expo app. The Next.js buyer, seller and admin web apps share the same Tailwind v4 tokens (POOL colours, spacing, Telugu and Hindi type scale), so the 5 developers write one design language on both platforms.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces NativeWind or StyleSheet-based styling.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free. An optional paid 'Uniwind Pro' adds a C++ ShadowTree engine, Reanimated className animations and native theme transitions; Pro pricing not verified.
gems.activity_evidence: 1,725 GitHub stars; v1.12.0 released 2026-09-04; last push 2026-09-29; about 1.04M weekly npm downloads.
gems.maturity_risk: Young (about 14 months old) and has a small core team. It requires Tailwind v4 and CSS-based theming. Its speed claims come from the vendor's own benchmarks.

gems.name: React Native Reusables (shadcn/ui for React Native)
gems.what_it_is: The shadcn/ui 'copy the source into your repo' model ported to React Native. It sits on rn-primitives, styled with NativeWind or Uniwind, and components are added with a CLI.
gems.why_gem: It was listed in the 2025 JS Rising Stars Mobile category (+3.3k stars). You own the component source, so Claude Code and the developers can read and edit it directly instead of fighting a black-box dependency. Its API mirrors web shadcn, so web and mobile components share names and props.
gems.use_in_pool: Base primitives for the mobile app: Button, Card, Dialog, Tabs, Select, Toggle and Progress for the pool card, the bid list and the accept/walk-away sheet. It keeps parity with the shadcn components used on the seller web dashboard.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces NativeBase (deprecated, which became gluestack), React Native Paper and RN Elements.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free
gems.activity_evidence: 8,674 stars; last push 2026-09-27; rn-primitives@1.4.0 released 2026-03-28; @react-native-reusables/cli 0.7.1 (2026-03-14).
gems.maturity_risk: Releases are infrequent: the last tagged release was March 2026, although commits are recent. The component set is smaller than web shadcn, so expect to write some components yourself.

gems.name: HeroUI Native
gems.what_it_is: A React Native component library from the HeroUI team (formerly NextUI), built on Tailwind v4 through Uniwind. Every component ships with animations and built-in accessibility.
gems.why_gem: It started in June 2025 and reached v1 recently (v1.0.10, 2026-09-21), so most teams have not seen it yet. HeroUI itself appears in the 2025 JS Rising Stars component libraries. It gives more 'polished out of the box' motion and detail than bare Reusables, on the same Uniwind engine.
gems.use_in_pool: A fast route to premium-feeling screens for the investor demo: animated chips, switches, accordions and sheets without hand-tuning each animation. Use it alongside Reusables or instead of it; pick one per screen family.
gems.replaces_or_adds: An alternative to React Native Reusables and Tamagui for polished animated components.
gems.license_or_pricing: Apache-2.0, free (no paid tier mentioned)
gems.activity_evidence: 3,664 stars; v1.0.10 released 2026-09-21; about 192k weekly npm downloads.
gems.maturity_risk: v1 is only months old. It is installed as a dependency, not copied in, so it is less editable than Reusables. It is tied to Uniwind.

gems.name: @expo/ui (native Jetpack Compose and SwiftUI from React Native), stable since SDK 56
gems.what_it_is: Real Jetpack Compose (Material 3) and SwiftUI components used from JavaScript through a single import, with a universal layer on top: Host, Row, Column, Text, TextInput, Button, Switch, Slider, Checkbox, BottomSheet and more. It includes Material 3 Dynamic Colors (useMaterialColors).

On low-end Android those feel native and cost less than JavaScript-animated look-alikes. It mixes with normal RN views, Skia and DOM components on the same screen.
gems.use_in_pool: System-native controls where 'feels like my phone' matters most for Tier-2/3 Android buyers: date and time pickers for the pool closing time, switches and sliders in settings, and a native bottom sheet for the bid-accept confirmation.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces the community datetimepicker, JavaScript-drawn switches and sliders, and some bottom-sheet libraries.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free

gems.name: Base UI v1.x (Drawer, OTPField, Combobox, NumberField, Toast)
gems.what_it_is: Unstyled, accessible React primitives from the MUI, Radix and Floating UI authors. v1.0.0 stable shipped 2025-12-11; it added Drawer in v1.2 (Feb 2026) and OTPField in v1.4 (stable by v1.6). shadcn now offers Base UI as a primitive option.

gems.use_in_pool: On the web and PWA: OTPField for the delivery/pickup handover code and phone OTP; Combobox for the 'paste link or search product' box; NumberField for seller bid entry; Drawer as the mobile-web bottom sheet; Toast for 'someone joined your pool'.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces Radix UI plus Vaul plus input-otp as separate dependencies.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free

gems.name: shadcn CLI 3-4: registries, MCP server, private GitHub registries (plus tweakcn for theming)
gems.what_it_is: shadcn is no longer 'just copy components'. CLI 3.0 (Aug 2025) added namespaced registries and an MCP server. Oct 2025 added a registry directory plus Field, InputGroup, Item, Spinner and Empty. Dec 2025 added `npx shadcn create`. Jan 2026 added RTL. Aug 2026 added private GitHub registries and a Questionnaire (multi-step form) component. tweakcn is a free visual theme editor for shadcn (Rising Stars 2025).
